title: Error-correcting codes for logical expert addresses
hypothesis: For a fixed bank of 16 distinct experts, Hamming(7,4) addresses will reduce wrong-route rate at p=.05 bit corruption to <=0.06 versus raw 4-bit IDs, with full inference payload <=1.01x raw-ID payload, in both development seeds.
physical_object: one fixed shared bank of 16 linear expert matrices, paid in every address method
mirror_coordinate: raw, random, Hamming ECOC or repeated-bit expert address
logical_multiplicity: 16 callable experts, each chosen by an incoming logical expert ID

task.type: synthetic routed expert function bank with controlled address-channel bit flips
task.channel: independent Bernoulli bit flips per address bit
task.quality: wrong expert rate and output RMSE against the requested expert's linear output

storage.authority: actual uncompressed NPZ inference payload bytes

gates.PROMISING: At p=.05, Hamming(7,4) route error <=0.06 and actual serialized payload <=1.01x raw-ID payload in both seeds; no-confusion output replay passes. Any robustness also achieved by a same-bit native code is not Mirror-specific.
gates.FAIL: The independent no-noise upper is valid, but the frozen reliability/byte gate fails or standard native ECOC explains the robustness tradeoff without a Mirror-specific gain.
gates.NOT ESTABLISHED: No-noise expert output replay fails or serialized metrics do not replay.

boundaries: This isolates address corruption on a synthetic linear expert bank; it does not establish learned-router robustness.
Every redundant address bit and codebook byte is charged.
No codeword combinations are counted as additional experts.
Fresh seeds remain sealed unless gates pass and native attribution is resolved.
